integrity: The forward implication is a direct sign-symmetry argument. The converse converts the conditional-mean identity into an exponential transform identity, factors it using independence, and forces the centered moment generating function to be even near zero; uniqueness then gives central symmetry. An exact finite-support census is supplementary rather than inferential.
scientific_limitations: The converse is proved under local existence of the moment generating function; weaker transform assumptions are not claimed.
The theorem characterizes central symmetry, not full independence of midpoint and range or normality.
The sample size is exactly two; no larger-sample range characterization is asserted.
An older midrange-characterization article was only accessible at abstract level and remains a residual originality risk.
title: A flat midpoint–separation regression characterizes symmetry
